pages.title: Start here: how this workspace runs

text.text: A ten-minute tour of the center in this workspace. Share it with the director, each lead teacher and whoever runs the front desk.
: each room's age group, capacity, ratio, teachers, lead and children enrolled.
: each child's room, schedule, subsidy, tuition owed and billed, review date, health record, allergy and care plan, and authorized pickup.
: every family from first call to enrolled, in fair order.
: monthly invoices, the subsidy share, and what is still owed.
: drills, inspections, certifications and logs, each with a due date.
Every morning: the opening checklist and staffing against ratios.
Monday: safety checks due this week; tours for the week confirmed.
Wednesday: waitlist calls for any opening; enrollment packets chased.
Friday: tuition due next week sent; overdue tuition followed up kindly.
Every morning: ratios in every room, checks due today
Every week: medication log review, overdue tuition, tours
Every month: fire drill, playground inspection, invoices sent
Every year: licensing renewal, staff certifications, room moves
The director owns enrollment, tuition and licensing. Lead teachers own their room, daily sheets and children's reviews. The front desk signs children in and out and checks pickup lists.

Invoices go out a week before the first of the month. When a state subsidy pays part, the invoice shows the subsidy share and the family's part separately, and the subsidy agency's attendance report is sent on time so payments are not held up.
Children appear here by first name and last initial. Allergy plans, pickup lists and tuition are confidential and shared only with staff who need them. Never put photos of children in this workspace.
Rename rooms, age groups and checks to match your license and delete the sample rows once your own are in. Edit any cell in place and drag cards between columns; every count updates on its own.
The center at a glance. Charts read the live tables.

text.text: Families hand you the most important people in their lives at 7:00 in the morning. The opening routine makes sure every room is safe, staffed and in ratio before the first child walks in.
Walk every classroom: outlets covered, no hazards on the floor, cribs clear of blankets and toys
Check the playground before anyone goes out: gates latched, surfacing in place, nothing sharp or broken
Fridge and freezer temperatures written in the log
Staff schedule against expected children in each room
(children per teacher) and the number of

. Common licensing limits are four infants, six toddlers, seven twos and ten preschoolers per adult, with smaller group sizes for the youngest; your state's rule is the one that counts. Count children at every transition: arrival, outdoor time, lunch, nap and pickup. If a room goes over, a floater or the director steps in at once.
Every child is signed in by an adult, with the time.
Medicine is handed to a teacher with a signed permission form, never left in a bag.
Release children only to an adult on the
list, with photo ID for anyone the staff do not know. A parent who wants someone new added must tell the office in writing. Custody orders on file are followed exactly.
Diaper changes, meals and naps written on each child's daily sheet.
Infants sleep on their backs, in a crib, with nothing else in it.
Any injury, however small, gets an incident report signed by the parent at pickup.
Every child signed out; the sign-in sheet matches
Rooms swept, toys sanitized, laundry started

At 7:40 the toddler room has nine children and one teacher because the second teacher's bus is late. The director moves the floater into the room until she arrives at 8:05, and notes the time in the staffing log.
Most centers have more families waiting than spaces. A fair, written waitlist and a warm enrollment process protect your reputation and keep every room full.
Every call or email becomes a row in
with the age group and the start date the family wants.

After the tour, families who want a space pay the waitlist fee and become
Write your rules down and follow them: siblings of enrolled children first, then children of staff, then by the date the family joined the list. Never skip a family because of who they are.
Look at the classroom's openings and the waitlist for that age group.
Call the first family in order and set them to
, with a deadline of three to five days.
If they decline, move to the next family the same day.
Immunization record or exemption on file; tick
Tuition agreement, deposit paid, and subsidy approval if the family has one
Start with two short visits with a parent, then a half day, then the full schedule. Infants and toddlers settle faster with a gradual start, and parents settle faster too.
to decide when they move to the next room. Moves happen together with the receiving teacher, after a few visits.

A space opens in the Saplings room. The director calls the Mbatha family, first on the twos waitlist, who accept the next day. Their packet is complete within a week, two short visits follow, and their daughter starts on the first of the month.
Licensing visits are unannounced. The center that is ready every day never fears one. Keep each check on a date in
and close it when it is done.
: monthly, at different times of day, including nap time. Write how long it took to get everyone out.
: daily walk-through, and a written inspection monthly.
: CPR and first aid current for every staff member; background checks before anyone starts.
: fridge temperatures daily; a kitchen review monthly.
: water, food, diapers, medicines and contact lists checked every quarter.
: weekly. Every dose given matches a signed permission form.
: the yearly renewal and any surprise visit; keep the file ready.
Staff files: background checks, training hours, CPR and first aid
Children's files: enrollment forms, immunizations, pickup lists, allergy plans
Drill logs, playground and kitchen logs, incident reports
Ratios and attendance records for the last three months
Each child's plan is posted (with the parent's permission) in their room and the kitchen. Medicines like epinephrine stay in the room and go outside with the group.
Every injury gets a written report the same day, signed by the parent at pickup. Anything serious is reported to licensing within your state's deadline.
Infants sleep on their backs in a crib with a fitted sheet and nothing else. Check sleeping infants every fifteen minutes and write it down.
Overdue checks in the Dashboard: none

A licensing visitor arrives on a Tuesday. The director opens the file: the last fire drill was three weeks ago, playground logs are current, and every child's immunization record is on file except one, already flagged and requested. The visit ends with no findings.
